key_insight: Atomistic simulations link alumina inclusion fraction and aluminum grain structure to effective elastic properties, strength, and failure behavior in aluminum-matrix nanocomposites.
engineering_relevance: The evaluated parameters can inform upper-scale constitutive models for particulate aluminum–alumina composites.
method: Molecular statics of a single alumina crystal embedded in aluminum, varying ceramic volume fraction.
Polycrystalline representative volume elements containing an alumina particle, varying aluminum grain count.
Tension–compression stress–strain analysis and comparison of isotropized elastic constants with Voigt–Reuss–Hill bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation of elastic moduli, ultimate strength, ultimate strain, and failure strain, alongside atomistic identification of deformation and fracture mechanisms, but provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Transferability to larger-scale engineering conditions requires validation beyond the atomistic models and loading conditions described.
paper_title: Evaluation of upper-scale mechanical parameters of particulate aluminum-based nanocomposites from molecular simulations
